text:
alex.k: Seeing intermittent 502s from the web console on /playground. Users report generation failing then succeeding a few seconds later. No clear pattern. Can someone share exact steps we want from the customer (HAR + console) and a quick curl repro we can ask for?

maria_s: Hi Alex — yes, please ask for a HAR export + console logs + the request_id from the failing request. Short checklist below. I'll paste a curl example you can ask them to run too.

alex.k: Thanks — want to paste that here so I can send it to the customer thread. Also what fields do we need in the support ticket?

maria_s: Copy/paste this to the customer: 
- Browser + version (e.g., Chrome 118.0.5993.90 on macOS 14.2)
- Exact time (UTC) you saw the error
- Steps to reproduce (minimal clicks)
- Attach: Network HAR (Save as HAR with content) + Console log capture (copy console or save as .txt)
- If possible, run the curl below and paste output and the `X-Request-Id` header value if present.

maria_s: Curl repro (replace placeholders):
```
# quick single-request repro (POST)
curl -i -X POST \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{"input":"hello"}' \ 
  https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate

# include a request-id header to force consistent id propagation (optional)
curl -i -X POST \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -H "X-Custom-Request-Id: my-test-1234" \ 
  -d '{"input":"hello"}' \ 
  https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate
```

maria_s: For the HAR + console instructions (short, step-by-step):
1) Open Chrome DevTools (F12 or Cmd+Option+I).
2) In Network tab: check "Preserve log" and "Disable cache".
3) Reproduce the issue (perform the request in the app).
4) Right-click anywhere in Network list -> "Save all as HAR with content" -> attach the .har.
5) Switch to Console tab, right-click -> "Save as..." (or select all and copy->paste into a .txt). Include the console timestamps.
6) If they see a failing network row, click it -> Headers -> look for response headers. Copy any `x-request-id`, `x-rid`, or `x-trace-id`.

maria_s: Additional tips to ask the user to include: the top-level request URL, status code, response body snapshot (if available), and screenshot of the UI error.

alex.k: This is perfect. One question: some users are on Safari — steps differ. Any short Safari notes?

samira.v: Safari notes: Web Inspector -> Network tab -> option to preserve log is at the top. Reproduce -> right-click -> "Export HAR". Console: Console tab -> right-click -> "Export". If they can't export, ask them to paste console lines and the failing request headers.

jordan.p: Also recommend asking for: a short curl with verbose trace to include wire-level details, e.g.:
```
curl -sS -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{"input":"hello"}' \ 
  https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate 2>&1 | sed -n '1,200p'
```
This will show request/response headers and any TLS negotiation noise that can hint at proxies.

alex.k: Great. I'll ping the customer with these steps. If they upload the HAR here, what's our intake flow?

supportbot: Please upload sensitive debug bundles to the secure upload endpoint: https://files.redwood.dev/upload and include the generated upload token in the ticket. Do NOT post HAR contents in public channels. :lock:

maria_s: After upload, add a comment in the ticket with the upload token and time range. Eng will pull the HAR into our repro harness and look for `x-request-id` matching our logs.

alex.k: FYI customer came back with one failing request id: req_20260317T154512Z_7f9b. They attached a HAR and console.txt to the upload link.

jordan.p: Thanks — I've started a search in the logs for `req_20260317T154512Z_7f9b`. If you can also provide the exact UTC timestamp from the customer's report (they gave 2026-03-17 15:45:12 UTC), that helps narrow it to the correct ingestion shard.

samira.v: Quick triage checklist for eng: check gateway 502s around that time, see if upstream model hosts reported OOM or restart, check routing fallback events, and confirm rate limits. We'll update the ticket once we match the request id.

alex.k: Awesome — closing loop with customer now. Thanks all :v:
